subject: english
question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose "No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I'm not __going to work__ today.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence **"I'm not going to work today." **is **grammatically correct **and **does not require any change**s.
 
• The structure of the sentence is appropriate for conveying the intended meaning.
 
• The use of the present continuous tense "I'm not going" is correct in this context.
 
• Therefore, no improvement is needed.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I'm not going to work today."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "go to work"** – This option changes the verb form and alters the intended meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3: "goes to work"** – This option is incorrect because it does not match the subject "I" in the sentence.
 
• **Option 4: "going to working"** – This option is grammatically incorrect.
